mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in housing starts over three consecutive months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% within a month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (below 1%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as cheap borrowing costs fuel economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative more than 40% of the time when FEDFUNDS is below 1%, or if the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) over one month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and a decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over one month signals a positive demand shock with controlled inflation, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases and CPIAUCSL decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of RSAFS increases and CPIAUCSL decreases on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month during a late-cycle expansion signals a supply-side slowdown, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met during a late-cycle expansion, or if the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in this specific regime.
